question: Prediction of progression from MCI to AD from structural MRI in ADNI MCI patients (P-182: baseline hippocampal box; P-78: whole-brain sMRI, one to four scans). Horizon (follow-up at least 18 months vs status at 36 months) and training (AD/CN transfer vs CDR-SB-supervised pretraining) differ, which the rule allows.
metric: Shared: accuracy with accuracy (the record's comparison); both also report AUC.

figures.P-182: 381 ADNI-2/GO MCI (118 pMCI, 263 sMCI), single baseline scan, model trained only on AD vs CN: accuracy 75.85%, Wilson n=381 -> 0.713-0.799 (centre 0.756, half-width 0.043); AUC 0.777, Hanley-McNeil Q1=0.635, Q2=0.680, SE=sqrt([0.777*0.223+117*(0.635-0.6037)+262*(0.680-0.6037)]/(118*263))=0.028 -> 0.723-0.831.
figures.P-78: Intervals reported (1000 bootstrap resamples). Internal Dataset B (101 held-out ADNI-1/2/GO subjects, 304 images; class split not reported): four scans (QTP) accuracy 0.907 (0.870-0.944), AUC 0.871 (0.805-0.926) - the record's figure; one scan (STP) accuracy 0.763 (0.711-0.816), AUC 0.832 (0.783-0.874). External Dataset A (baseline scan only; 29 ADNI-3 + 144 OASIS-3 subjects, 91 pMCI / 82 sMCI): accuracy 0.827 (0.769-0.884), AUC 0.858 (0.803-0.918). The Dataset B intervals are narrower than a subject-level interval for 101 subjects (Wilson for 0.763 at n=101: 0.671-0.835), which suggests resampling of images, not subjects.

matched_figure_check: P-78 reports the single-scan condition twice, with mixed results. (a) Internal Dataset B STP, the closest match (same ADNI-1/2/GO family, held-out ADNI subjects, one scan): accuracy 0.763 (0.711-0.816) contains 75.85%, and 0.763 lies inside P-182's 0.713-0.799 (z = 0.13), so the recorded 90.7 vs 75.85 gap dissolves. On AUC, 0.777 lies 0.006 below P-78's lower bound 0.783, and 0.832 lies 0.001 above P-182's derived upper bound 0.831 (z = 1.52): at the edge of the rule's test. (b) External Dataset A (one baseline scan, different cohort): accuracy 0.827 (0.769-0.884) vs 0.7585 (0.713-0.799) and AUC 0.858 (0.803-0.918) vs 0.777 (0.723-0.831) each exclude the other estimate (z = 1.87 and 2.01). So the four-scan headline gap is reconciled on the recorded metric, but a smaller single-scan gap (AUC about 0.83-0.86 vs 0.78; external accuracy 82.7% vs 75.85%) is not.

candidate_explanations.difference: Input representation (recorded gap only): the 90.7% needs four longitudinal scans; with one scan P-78's internal accuracy is 76.3%. This is shown by P-78 and dissolves the recorded accuracy gap.

candidate_explanations.difference: Training: P-182's model never saw MCI labels (AD/CN transfer from a hippocampal box); P-78's encoder is pretrained on CDR-SB across 1393 subjects and trained on longitudinal MCI data.

reason: The recorded gap (P-78 90.7% vs P-182 75.85%) comes from P-78's four-scan input. On one scan in the same ADNI family, P-78's accuracy is 76.3% (71.1-81.6%), matching P-182, so on the record's quantity the pair fails condition 3. But P-78's single-scan AUC (0.832 internal, at the edge of the rule's test; 0.858 external) and its external single-scan accuracy (82.7%) exceed P-182's figures beyond the rule's interval test. The matched figures therefore split, and the pair is borderline. If reported, it should be reported as this smaller single-scan discrepancy, not as 90.7 vs 75.85, with the training, horizon and cohort differences as candidate explanations that are not shown to be sufficient.
